title: VESPER Endpoint Capability Descriptor
description: REM-009 §4.2. What a surface can actually do, declared by the surface -- so that a scene producer never names an endpoint (INV-SCENE-4) and a renderer never requires a field outside the scene schema (INV-SCENE-1). `spatial_class` is the field that makes the projector and glass-cube targets first-class rather than special cases. Authority: SR-002, SR-018, SR-020, SR-028, SR-046, SR-047; REM-009, REM-011; DF-SELECT-ENDPOINT, DF-DEGRADE.

modalities.description: An endpoint with only audio_out is a legitimate, fully-supported target. A-026 boots the system with every text surface disabled and requires every core capability to remain reachable.

spatial_class.description: The rung this endpoint occupies on every element's degradation ladder. `none` is voice-only and is the row that forces the scene schema to carry what a diagram MEANS rather than an image of it -- a rendered PNG cannot be narrated; a typed graph can.

text_capacity.description: Characters comfortably legible at the expected viewing distance. Null for audio-only. Zero is meaningful and distinct from null: a state-indicator LED has visual modality and zero text capacity.

barge_in_supported.description: REM-010 latency budget: barge-in honoured within 200 ms. An endpoint that cannot be interrupted is a degradation to report, not a fact to hide.

interaction_classes.description: `physical_button` matters disproportionately: INV-ALARM-2 requires at least one acknowledgment channel that is physical and ASR-INDEPENDENT. A wake-up that can only be dismissed by speaking fails for a person who has just woken up.

privacy_class.description: DF-SELECT-ENDPOINT input. The fail-safe: unknown person present, or user_location_confidence below threshold, routes to the most private available surface or WITHHOLDS. Never defaults to the most public surface -- the natural implementation routes to the largest display, which is the projector, which is the one a guest can read (A-010 negative control).

space_ref.description: Topological space reference (INV-WORLD-2). No subsystem requires metric coordinates; `spatial_intent` on a scene is relational and resolves against this graph at render time.

availability_class.description: REM-011 / REM-014. Separates TRUST from AVAILABILITY -- the correction OWNER-DECISION-002 produced. A node can be fully trusted (Z0) and only intermittently awake; fusing the two is what previously excluded the phone entirely. INV-TRUST-2 constrains PLANNED assignment to foreground_only endpoints; it does not forbid runtime survival on one.

measured_at_hlc.description: Capabilities are DISCOVERED and re-measured, not configured once. An endpoint whose descriptor is older than its re-attestation interval is treated as UNKNOWN, and UNKNOWN endpoints are not selected.

then.$comment: An endpoint with no spatial class and no non-visual modality can render nothing, and would silently swallow every scene routed to it.
A public surface must be locatable in the space graph, or the privacy fail-safe cannot reason about who can see it.

$comment: EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: fonts, colours, pixel dimensions, CSS, and any styling vocabulary. Those belong to the renderer. If a scene producer could read them it would begin producing layouts, and the endpoint-independence property -- the one that makes voice, projector and volumetric outputs the same architecture -- would be gone within a sprint.
